title: Finding a file
bodyMd:
A fictional research office replaced shared paper folders with a searchable digital archive. Staff expected searches to become faster. The first review found that familiar documents were easy to retrieve, but documents described with inconsistent names were often missed. A report labelled “annual water use” did not always appear in searches for “yearly consumption.”

The office introduced a small shared vocabulary and allowed several descriptive terms for each file. It also kept examples showing how different teams referred to the same subject. The aim was not to force everyone to write in identical language. It was to connect varied language to a common retrieval system. Digitization had changed where records were stored, but useful access still depended on decisions about description, classification and the questions users were likely to ask.
